image_description: A high-angle shot of a group of six hamsters huddled together on wood shaving bedding. The group includes adults and pups with varying coat patterns: golden/orange, black and white (pied), and tricolor. They are arranged in a loose cluster, some sleeping, some awake.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Broad head with prominent cheek pouches extending to shoulders.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central golden hamster clearly displays the characteristic broad head and swollen cheek pouches typical of the species.
Visible eyes on the awake hamsters are small, round, and dark, consistent with hamster anatomy.
Ears are visible as small, rounded flaps on the sides of the heads, proportionate to the body size.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Stocky compact body with diminutive, rounded proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All subjects exhibit the classic ovoid, stocky body shape of hamsters without elongation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dense short fur in golden, brown, black, or white coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Fur texture appears dense and short. Colors match the allowed palette (golden, black, white patches).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short legs with clawed digits; hind feet slightly elongated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Legs are largely tucked under bodies or occluded by other hamsters/bedding. Digits are not resolvable at this resolution.
Tails are either hidden beneath bodies or too small to be distinguished from the surrounding fur and bedding in this cluster.

artifact_observations.location: Contact points between hamsters, specifically the top-left golden hamster and the one below it.
artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight blurring and merging of fur textures where bodies touch, making individual boundaries indistinct. Common in AI generation but also possible in low-res photography.
Bedding lacks distinct structural variety; some shavings appear to melt into the background or have inconsistent lighting/shadows.
The rear anatomy is ambiguous; the transition from body to hindquarters lacks clear definition, appearing somewhat 'melted' into the bedding.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm species identification and rule out misclassification as mice or rats.
To verify limb count and structural integrity of the most visible subject.
To detect fusion artifacts between overlapping bodies and separate subjects from bedding.
To assess overall coherence, lighting consistency, and subtle texture anomalies.

focus_areas: Anatomical correctness of paws/digits if visible
Consistency of fur texture across different subjects
